facts.text: Hybrid is the 10th film in Syfy's Maneater series, a run of made-for-TV creature features. Most were shot in Winnipeg, Manitoba, which is also where this one was filmed.
Director Yelena Lanskaya's Hallmark Channel movies Hidden Places and The Colt ranked among the network's 2nd and 17th most-watched telecasts ever, per her bio.
Lead Cory Monteith (Aaron Scates) later became Finn Hudson on Glee. Hybrid was his first starring role, per Wikipedia's career summary and press bios.
Justine Bateman (Dr. Andrea Hewlitt) is the older sister of Jason Bateman, and daughter of actor Kent Bateman. Both siblings were child TV stars.
Before acting, Cory Monteith (Aaron Scates) worked as a Walmart Canada greeter, taxi driver, mechanic, school bus driver, roofer and band drummer.
The villainous research lab in the story, the Olaris Institute, is set in Winnipeg, the same Manitoba city where the movie was actually shot, per Craig J. Clark's Werewolf News review.
Cory Monteith (Aaron Scates) won his Glee role partly with a tape of himself drumming on pencils and plastic tubs. Producers then asked for a singing tape, and he sent a cover of REO Speedwagon.
Screenwriter Arne Olsen's credits go from this wolf-eyed thriller to the animated sequel All Dogs Go to Heaven 2, plus Red Scorpion and Cop and a Half.
Cory Monteith (Aaron Scates) shared in a 2009 Screen Actors Guild Award for Glee's ensemble, two years after playing a wolf-eyed man in this Sci Fi Channel movie.
Foywonder of Dread Central gave Hybrid 1.5 out of 5 and called it basically The Eye with a lycanthrope twist, though he credited it for going the psychological-thriller route.
The screenplay is by Arne Olsen, who also wrote Red Scorpion (1988), Cop and a Half (1993) and the Mighty Morphin Power Rangers movie.
Dread Central's Foywonder said the movie leans on nature footage and montages of wolves to fill out its roughly 90 minutes.
Justine Bateman (Andrea) is the Mallory from Family Ties. She left acting from 2000 to 2003 to run a fashion label that sold to Saks Fifth Avenue.
Brandon Jay McLaren (Ashmore) went to the University at Albany on a soccer scholarship before turning to acting.
Justine Bateman (Andrea) later earned a computer science degree from UCLA in 2016. In 2021 she made her feature directing debut with Violet, starring Olivia Munn.
DVD Talk's Stephen Hawco called Hybrid 'cheap, uncaptivating horror,' said the wolf cutaways get ridiculous, and speculated it may have been shot on mini-DV video.
The 'futuristic truck' in this film is the Landmaster from Damnation Alley (1977). It is a one-off 12-wheeled armored vehicle that cost about $350,000 to build in 1976.
IMDb's connections list Hybrid as referencing the 2001 comedy The Animal, another movie about a man changed by borrowed animal parts.
The Landmaster was built by Dean Jeffries and sat beside his North Hollywood shop for decades. It was sold to a private owner in 2005 and restored, two years before it showed up in Hybrid.
Horror Bob (Robert Brodmerkel) called Hybrid a low-budget horror with 'an eighties direct-to-video feel' and one of the better Maneater series films he'd seen.
The Landmaster has had a busy afterlife: a Quiet Riot video, an Amoco ad, Highway to Heaven, Get a Life, and the Shin Megami Tensei: Strange Journey video game.
Gordon Tootoosis (Grandpa) was named to the Order of Canada in 2004. He was a Cree actor and activist who also voiced Sheriff Gordy in Open Season (2006).
Gordon Tootoosis (Grandpa) said, 'Leadership is about submission to duty, not elevation to power.' He descended from Yellow Mud Blanket, brother of Cree leader Poundmaker.
Gordon Tootoosis (Grandpa) was the son of John Tootoosis, a founder of the National Indian Brotherhood. He also acted in Legends of the Fall (1994) and The Edge (1997).
Director Yelena Lanskaya also directed episodes of Law & Order: SVU. Her Hallmark film Hidden Places, starring Shirley Jones, won a 2007 CAMIE Award.
Brandon Jay McLaren (Ashmore) had been the Red Ranger in Power Rangers S.P.D. in 2005. Screenwriter Arne Olsen had earlier written the Power Rangers movie.
Blogger Rob of Newspaper Rock praised the film's Native actors and real wolves but argued the 'Indian werewolf' trope, already used in Twilight, reinforces stereotypes of Native people as savage.
Brandon Jay McLaren (Ashmore) later appeared in Tucker & Dale vs. Evil (2010) and the TV series Graceland, Falling Skies and Slasher.
Tinsel Korey (Lydia) went on to play Emily Young in The Twilight Saga: New Moon (2009). She also writes and performs her own music.
Tinsel Korey (Lydia) is best known as Emily Young in the Twilight films, though Wikipedia notes scholars have written that she falsely adopted a Native American identity.
Hybrid premiered on the Sci Fi Channel on August 14, 2007. The channel was later renamed Syfy.
The Maneater deal was announced in October 2006. The first six films premiered on Canada's Movie Central on Demand before airing on Syfy, because of a pre-licensing agreement.
Craig J. Clark of Werewolf News called Hybrid surprisingly tame. He said the cast plays an absurd story far too seriously and joked that its 90 minutes are time you won't get back.
Hybrid was produced by Paquin Entertainment Group and RHI Entertainment. RHI's financial problems put the Maneater series on hold after 2011.
Cory Monteith (Aaron Scates) died July 13, 2013, aged 31. Glee honored him with a tribute at the 2013 Emmy Awards.
A different movie also titled Hybrid (1997), directed by Fred Olen Ray, features the same Landmaster vehicle that this film borrows from Damnation Alley.
